# Purpose of this session {#purpose-of-this-session}

This file describes the different steps to perform the **third part** of the **single cell RNAseq** data analysis training course for the **EB3I n1 2026**, covering these steps :

-   **Filter out** cells that do not pass the filter quality
-   Calculate the **Cell cycle scoring** and asses the **Cell cycle state** of cells
-   Detect **doublets** from your data

**Input data**: the Seurat object with metrics calculated in the previous session. `02_TD3A_S5_Metrics_31053.4587.RDS`

**Output data**: saved in your `RESULTS` directory:

| File | Content |
|:------------------------------------|:----------------------------------|
| `03_TD3A_S5_Metrics.Filtered_12508.4278.RDS` | filtered for unwanted cells and genes |
| `04_TD3A_S5_CC_12508.4278.RDS` | \+ Cell cycle prediction |
| `05_TD3A_S5_Doublets.Filtered_12508.4278.RDS` | filtered for detected doublets |

We also prepare a small function to save the objects of this session with the naming convention of the course (step number, sample, step name, object dimension):

```{r}
#| label: save_func
#| filename: save_func

save_step <- function(object, step_number, step_name) {
  out_name <- paste0(
    output_dir, "/",
    paste(
      c(step_number, Seurat::Project(object), "S5", step_name,
        paste(dim(object), collapse = ".")),
      collapse = "_"),
    ".RDS")
  saveRDS(object = object, file = out_name)
  message("Saved [", out_name, "]")
}
```

For example, `save_step(sobj, "05", "Doublet.Filtered")` will write `05_TD3A_S5_Doublet.Filtered_12508.4035.RDS`.

# Filtering

## Features

-   As already explained, the **sparsity** of the count matrix is high, *very* high.

-   To the point that there probably are some features that have **so low expression** level that they were only counted in **very few cells**. As such, they have absolutely **no chance** to characterize any cell type, nor harbor some variation between different cell types.

-   As such, we should **discard** these features

<br>

What are the actual dimensions of our expression data ?

```{r}
#| label: dim1
#| filename: dim1

## Dimensions of our Seurat object
dim(sobj)

```

<br>

We want to remove the features that are expressed in less than **`r min_cells`** cells.

First, we quantify, for each feature, the number of cells with `0` count.

```{r}
#| label: Ncell_no_exp
#| filename: Ncell_no_exp

## Compute the amount of 0s per feature
nFeat_zero <- sparseMatrixStats::rowCounts(
  x = SeuratObject::GetAssayData(
    object = sobj, 
    assay = "RNA", 
    layer = "counts"), 
  value = 0)

## Inversion : computing the number of cells with at least one count, per feature
nFeat_nonzero <- ncol(sobj) - nFeat_zero

## Identify those with at least 5 cells with expression
nFeat_keep <- nFeat_nonzero >= min_cells

## Quantify the selected ones
table(nFeat_keep)

```

<br>

And now we can **discard** features expressed in less than `r min_cells` cells :

<br>

```{r}
#| label: remove_gene_no_exp
#| filename: remove_gene_no_exp

## Create a temporary object for the DEMO part
sobj_VIZ_pre <- sobj

## Restrict the Seurat object
sobj <- subset(x = sobj, features = rownames(sobj)[nFeat_keep])

```

<br>

What are the Seurat object dimensions, now ?

```{r}
#| label: dim2
#| filename: dim2

dim(sobj)

```

<br>

::: {.callout-important icon="false" style="background: pink"}
### DEMO - See the effect of gene removal on UMAP

We can **visualize the cell space** before and after this features filtering.

```{r}
#| label: prefeatfiltviz
#| filename: prefeatfiltviz

## Usual set of "U can't C me" functions
sobj_VIZ_pre <- Seurat::NormalizeData(object = sobj_VIZ_pre, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_VIZ_pre <- Seurat::ScaleData(object = sobj_VIZ_pre, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_VIZ_pre <- Seurat::FindVariableFeatures(object = sobj_VIZ_pre, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_VIZ_pre <- Seurat::RunPCA(object = sobj_VIZ_pre, npcs = 21, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_VIZ_pre <- Seurat::RunUMAP(object = sobj_VIZ_pre, dims = c(1:20), verbose = FALSE)

## Cell space visualization
dp_pre <- Seurat::DimPlot(
  object = sobj_VIZ_pre, 
  reduction = 'umap')
print(dp_pre)

## Remove temporary object
rm(sobj_VIZ_pre)
```

```{r}

#| filename: postfeatfiltviz

## Usual set of "U can't C me" functions
```

# Cell cycle scores

-   We are currently analyzing **independent** profiles from **isolated** cells, from a sample dissociation

-   As such, cells were most probably **not synchronized**, thus the effect of their **cell cycle state** on genes expression may be strong, to the point that it can **bias the data** (ie, mask some lower amplitude biological variation).

-   In order to **assess** (and maybe, *remove*) this bias, we have to **quantify** it.

-   We will perform this estimation thanks to heuristics based on **knowledge** : Seurat includes a method that evaluates the cell cycle phase of cells through **scores for the S and G2M phases**, each based on phase-specific **gene signatures**.

-   For this step, we will use additional gene lists from [ ](TODO%20:%20add%20paper%20reference). It was made on mouse data but can be used for human by determining ortholog genes.

## Load gene lists

We will directly download data from Zenodo :

```{r}
#| label: cc_load
#| filename: cc_load

## Copy the file into the DATA directory
sobj_file <- "mus_musculus_Seurat_cc.genes_20191031.rds"
sobj_path <- paste0(TD_dir, "/03_Preproc.3/DATA/", sobj_file)  # <1>

zenodo_get_data(file_name = sobj_file, zenodo_id = "14101506", local_path = input_dir)

## Load the file
cc_genes <- readRDS(file = sobj_path)
cc_genes

```

<br>

::: {.callout-note icon="false" style="background: lightblue"}
### QUESTION

As explained, we will use gene lists extracted from community knowledge. Our data contain values for genes also, so we will cross them.

Is there something we should check ?
:::

::: {.callout-note icon="false" collapse="true" style="background: lightgreen"}
### ANSWER

We may check if the genes in our gene lists are effectively present in our Seurat object !
:::

<br>

::: {.callout-warning icon="false" collapse="true" style="background: yellow"}
### OPTIONAL EXERCISE

1.  Write a code that performs this check

2.  Add a code to adjust the content of the gene lists accordingly (remove genes from the gene lists that are not present in our dataset) *(NOTE : this is actually not needed as already checked and corrected by the cell cyle estimation method we will use)*
:::

::: {.callout-warning icon="false" collapse="true" style="background: orange"}
### OPTIONAL ANSWER

```{r}
#| label: b_cc_answer
#| filename: b_cc_answer
#| eval: FALSE

## Check if our data genes cover the gene lists
lapply(cc_genes, function(x) x %in% rownames(sobj))

## Remove genes not in sobj
cc_genes <- lapply(cc_genes, function(gl) { gl[gl %in% rownames(sobj)] })

## Check the modification
str(cc_genes)

## Check that all genes are available in sobj
all(unique(unlist(cc_genes)) %in% rownames(sobj))

```
:::

<br>

## Estimation

Let's perform this estimation. But how ? It is calculated using the function `CellCycleScoring()` from the `Seurat` package.

```{r}
#| label: h_CellCycleScoring
#| filename: h_CellCycleScoring
#| eval: FALSE

## Reading the function help page
?Seurat::CellCycleScoring

```

```{r}
#| label: cc_run
#| filename: cc_run

## Creating a temporary object
sobj_CCS <- sobj

## Needs normalized counts to work. You will talk about it after.
sobj_CCS <- Seurat::NormalizeData(object = sobj_CCS, verbose = FALSE)

## Perform the estimation
set.seed(my_seed)
sobj_CCS <- Seurat::CellCycleScoring(
  object = sobj_CCS, 
  s.features = cc_genes$s.genes, 
  g2m.features = cc_genes$g2m.genes, 
  # assay = 'RNA, ## Seurat v4
  layer = 'RNA', ## Seurat v5
  nbin = 24, 
  seed = my_seed)
```

Results are stored in the metadata of the temporary object we created. We can see the content : 

```{r}
#| label: cc_result
#| filename: cc_result

head(sobj_CCS[[]][, c("S.Score", "G2M.Score", "Phase")])
```

This table contains a score for S and G2/M phases. It the assess the cell cycle state based on those scores. We can visualize the results as violins:

```{r}
#| label: vlncc
#| filename: vlncc

Seurat::VlnPlot(object = sobj_CCS,
                features = c("S.Score",
                             "G2M.Score"),
                group.by = "Phase")

```

Those restults are then transfered from the temporary object to the original Seurat object.

```{r}
#| label: cc_transfer
#| filename: cc_transfer

## Transfering score from the temp object to the real one
sobj$CC_Seurat_S.Score <- sobj_CCS$S.Score
sobj$CC_Seurat_G2M.Score <- sobj_CCS$G2M.Score
sobj$CC_Seurat_Phase <- as.factor(sobj_CCS$Phase)

## Add "S minus G2M" score
sobj$CC_Seurat_SmG2M.Score <- sobj$CC_Seurat_S.Score - sobj$CC_Seurat_G2M.Score

## Discard temp object
rm(sobj_CCS)
```

<br>

::: {.callout-important icon="false" style="background: pink"}
## DEMO - Visualise the cell cycle on UMAP

```{r}

#| filename: vizccp

## Usual set of "U can't C me" functions

sobj_VIZ_cc <- Seurat::ScaleData(object = sobj_VIZ_cc, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_VIZ_cc <- Seurat::FindVariableFeatures(object = sobj_VIZ_cc, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_VIZ_cc <- Seurat::RunPCA(object = sobj_VIZ_cc, npcs = 21, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_VIZ_cc <- Seurat::RunUMAP(object = sobj_VIZ_cc, dims = c(1:20), verbose = FALSE)
```

# Cell doublets

We will use **two different methods** to detect and remove cell doublets :

-   [`scds`](https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/scds.html){target="_blank"} (in its "hybrid" mode) : more efficient at detecting **homotypic** doublets

-   [`scDblFinder`](https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/scDblFinder.html){target="_blank"} : more efficient at detecting **heterotypic** doublets

None of the methods accepts a `SeuratObject` as input, but a [`SingleCellExperiment`](https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/SingleCellExperiment.html){target="_blank"} object.

Hopefully :

-   Seurat has a function to perform the conversion
-   The output results can be integrated into our Seurat object with ease

## Two methods

First, we create the SingleCellExperiment object.
```{r}
#| label: singleCellExperiment
#| filename: singleCellExperiment

sce_obj <- Seurat::as.SingleCellExperiment(sobj, assay = "RNA")
sce_obj
```

::: {.panel-tabset}
### `scds`

Let’s perform the doublet prediction using `scds` package and its `cxds_bcds_hybrid` function.

```{r}
#| label: scds_h
#| filename: scds_h
#| eval: False

## Show help message of the function cxds_bcds_hybrid
?scds::cxds_bcds_hybrid

```

```{r}
#| label: scds
#| filename: scds

## Fix seed
set.seed(my_seed)

## Run scds
sce_obj <- scds::cxds_bcds_hybrid(sce_obj)

```

The results are saved in the metadata of the object. This object is a SingleCellExperiment, not a Seurat object. To access the metadata, it uses the function `colData()`.

```{r}
#| label: scds_result
#| filename: scds_result

## Print metadata
head(colData(sce_obj)[, c("cxds_score", "bcds_score", "hybrid_score")])
```

We then transfer the results from the SingleCellExperiment object to the original Seurat object.

```{r}
#| label: scds_transfer
#| filename: scds_transfer

## Transfer results to Seurat object
scds.hybrid_is_doublet <- colData(sce_obj)[,"hybrid_score"]>1
sobj[[]][names(scds.hybrid_is_doublet),"doublet_scds.hybrid"] <- scds.hybrid_is_doublet

## Contingencies
table(sobj$doublet_scds.hybrid)
```

### `scDblFinder`

Let’s perform the doublet prediction using `scDblFinder` package and its `scDblFinder` function.

```{r}
#| label: scdbl_h
#| filename: scdbl_h
#| eval: False

?scDblFinder::scDblFinder

```

```{r}
#| label: scdbl
#| filename: scdbl

## Fix seed
set.seed(my_seed)

## Run scDblFinder
scDblFinder_results <- scDblFinder::scDblFinder(sce = sce_obj, returnType = "table")

```

The results are saved in a table. 

```{r}
#| label: scdbl_result
#| filename: scdbl_result

## Show results
head(scDblFinder_results)

## Keep only true cells and remove artificial doublets
scDblFinder_results <- scDblFinder_results[scDblFinder_results$type == "real",]
```

We then transfer the results from the table to our original Seurat object.

```{r}
#| label: scdbl_transfer
#| filename: scdbl_transfer

## Transfer results to seurat object
sobj[[]][rownames(scDblFinder_results), "doublet_scDblFinder"] <- scDblFinder_results$class == "doublet"

## Contingencies
table(sobj$doublet_scDblFinder)

```
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<br>

## Merge results

We merge results of the two methods

```{r}
#| label: dblmerge
#| filename: dblmerge

## Logical union of both methods
sobj$doublet_union <- sobj$doublet_scds.hybrid | sobj$doublet_scDblFinder

## Quantify doublets
table(sobj$doublet_union)

```

<br>

We can assess **tool-specific** and **common** doublets

```{r}
#| label: dbl_types
#| filename: dbl_types

### Singlets by default
sobj$doublet_viz <- "singlet"

### Union
sobj$doublet_viz[sobj$doublet_union] <- "both"

### scds-specific
sobj$doublet_viz[sobj$doublet_scds.hybrid & !sobj$doublet_scDblFinder] <- "scds"

### scDblFinder-specific
sobj$doublet_viz[sobj$doublet_scDblFinder & !sobj$doublet_scds.hybrid] <- "scDblFinder"

## Convert to factor
sobj$doublet_viz <- as.factor(sobj$doublet_viz)

## Contingencies
table(sobj$doublet_viz)

```

<br>

::: {.callout-warning icon="false" collapse="true" style="background: yellow"}
### OPTIONAL EXERCISE

Create an upset-plot for the doublet status according to the two methods used
:::

::: {.callout-warning icon="false" collapse="true" style="background: orange"}
### OPTIONAL ANSWER

```{r}
#| label: b_upset
#| filename: b_upset
#| eval: FALSE

## Build a list of cells tagged by one tool, the other, or both
dbl_list <-list(
  "scds" = colnames(sobj)[sobj$doublet_scds.hybrid],
  "scDblFinder" = colnames(sobj)[sobj$doublet_scDblFinder])

## Draw the upset plot
UpSetR::upset(data = UpSetR::fromList(dbl_list), 
              nintersects = NA, 
              sets = rev(names(dbl_list)),
              keep.order = TRUE,
              order.by = "freq")

```
:::

<br>

## Doublets filtering {.tabset .tabset-fade .tabset-pills}

Now we can remove barcodes identified as cell doublets, and visualize the cell space before and after.

```{r}
#| label: dblrm
#| filename: dblrm

## Dimensions before removal
dim(sobj)

## Create a temporary object
sobj_VIZ_dbl <- sobj

## Perform the removal
# sobj <- sobj[,!sobj$doublet_union]
sobj <- subset(
  x = sobj, 
  cells = colnames(sobj)[sobj$doublet_union], 
  invert = TRUE)

## Dimensions after
dim(sobj)

```

::: {.callout-important icon="false" style="background: pink"}
## DEMO - See effect of doublet removal

### BEFORE

```{r}
#| label: dblviz1
#| filename: dblviz1

### Doublets viz (before removal)

## Usual set of "U can't C me" functions
sobj_VIZ_dbl <- Seurat::NormalizeData(object = sobj_VIZ_dbl, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_VIZ_dbl <- Seurat::ScaleData(object = sobj_VIZ_dbl, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_VIZ_dbl <- Seurat::FindVariableFeatures(object = sobj_VIZ_dbl, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_VIZ_dbl <- Seurat::RunPCA(object = sobj_VIZ_dbl, npcs = 21, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_VIZ_dbl <- Seurat::RunUMAP(object = sobj_VIZ_dbl, dims = c(1:20), verbose = FALSE)

## Doublets visualization
dp_dbl <- Seurat::DimPlot(
  object = sobj_VIZ_dbl, 
  reduction = 'umap',
  group.by = 'doublet_viz')

## Plot
print(dp_dbl)

## Discard temp object
rm(sobj_VIZ_dbl)

```

### AFTER

```{r}
#| label: dblviz2
#| filename: dblviz2

### Doublets viz (after removal)

## Create a temporary object
sobj_VIZ_dbl <- sobj

## Usual set of "U can't C me" functions
sobj_VIZ_dbl <- Seurat::NormalizeData(object = sobj_VIZ_dbl, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_VIZ_dbl <- Seurat::ScaleData(object = sobj_VIZ_dbl, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_VIZ_dbl <- Seurat::FindVariableFeatures(object = sobj_VIZ_dbl, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_VIZ_dbl <- Seurat::RunPCA(object = sobj_VIZ_dbl, npcs = 21, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_VIZ_dbl <- Seurat::RunUMAP(object = sobj_VIZ_dbl, dims = c(1:20), verbose = FALSE)

## Doublets-filtered visualization
dp_dblf <- Seurat::DimPlot(
  object = sobj_VIZ_dbl, 
  reduction = 'umap',
  group.by = 'doublet_viz')

## Plot
print(dp_dblf)

## Discard temp object
rm(sobj_VIZ_dbl)

```

Merge plots for ease of use :

```{r dbl_umaps, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 6, class.source = "notrun", class.output="notruno"}
#| label: dbl_umaps
#| filename: dbl_umaps

## Using the patchwork package to merge plots (and ggplot2 to add titles)
patchwork::wrap_plots(
  list(
    dp_dbl & ggplot2::ggtitle(label = "Cell doublets (unfiltered)"),
    dp_dblf & ggplot2::ggtitle(label = "Cell doublets (filtered)")), 
  nrow = 1)

```
:::

<br>

::: {.callout-note icon="false" style="background: lightblue"}
### QUESTION

What do you observe when comparing before and after the doublets filtering ?
:::

::: {.callout-note icon="false" collapse="true" style="background: lightgreen"}
### ANSWER

Actually not that much !

This is due to the fact that this dataset did not contain a lot of heterotypic doublets

When a dataset is heavily contaminated with lots of heterotypic doublets, their removal can drastically remodel the topology.
:::
